items.abstract: <jats:p>Industrial surface-inspection systems usually return anomaly scores, classification labels, or segmentation masks, but operators often need direct answers to repeated visual questions: whether a defect is present, what morphology is visible, where it appears, how large its visible extent is, and whether the case should be reviewed. General vision-language models can express such answers, but their compute cost and weak grounding are poorly matched to a fixed-camera edge station. This paper presents Tiny Defect-VQA, a bounded visual question answering system for industrial image interpretation under explicit latency and memory limits. The data engine converts published defect labels and pixel masks into image-disjoint question-answer records using a versioned inspection ontology. The model combines a MobileNetV3-Small visual encoder, a compact two-layer question encoder, mask-guided question pooling, and low-rank gated fusion to predict both a typed answer and a defect heatmap. Post-hoc temperature scaling and question-specific thresholds route uncertain predictions to manual review. Under a locked five-fold protocol, Tiny Defect-VQA achieves 89.6% mean answer accuracy, 87.8% macro-F1, and 61.3% mask IoU, improving over the best matched compact baseline by 5.1 percentage points in accuracy and 5.7 points in macro-F1. Question-specific abstention reduces selective risk to 2.7% at 80% automatic-answer coverage. End-to-end Jetson Nano profiling reports 28.4 ms median latency and 431 MB peak memory, satisfying the declared 50-ms and 512-MB edge limits. These results position Tiny Defect-VQA as a quantitative, mask-grounded interface for real-world edge surface inspection.</jats:p>
title: Tiny Defect-VQA: Mask-Grounded Edge Visual Question Answering for Industrial Surface Inspection

items.abstract: <jats:p>Bridge inspections are a vital part of bridge maintenance and the main information source for Bridge Management Systems is used in decision-making regarding repairs. Without a doubt, both can benefit from the implementation of the Building Information Modelling philosophy. To fully harness the BIM potential in this area, we have to develop tools that will provide inspection accurate information easily and fast. In this paper, we present an example of how such a tool can utilise tablets coupled with the latest generation RGB-D cameras for data acquisition; how these data can be processed to extract the defect surface area and create a 3D representation, and finally embed this information into the BIM model. Additionally, the study of depth sensor accuracy is presented along with surface area accuracy tests and an exemplary inspection of a bridge pillar column.</jats:p>
title: The measurements of surface defect area with an RGB-D camera for a BIM-backed bridge inspection

items.abstract: Thermal infrared imaging is physically well-suited to industrial anomaly detection. However, calibrated thermal cameras cost thousands of dollars per device, making it inaccessible for most industrial environments. In this paper, we directly address this barrier. We prove that Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, establishes thermal emissivity and optical reflectance are complementary quantities at thermal equilibrium. Since luminance approximates reflectance for Lambertian surfaces, the synthetic thermal proxy ε = 1 – L follows directly from standard RGB input. This proxy is validated against physics-based IR references using r = 0.785 average Pearson correlation across a range of industrial surfaces. We propose ThermalCLIP, which combines this proxy with frozen CLIP ViT-B/16 patch features and PDE-based multiscale residuals. The core finding is that on surface categories where thermal diffusion structure is the primary discriminative signal, highly repetitive textures where all appearance-based patch features are near-identical, the physics-informed Laplacian residual provides information that appearance-based methods are structurally unable to recover. On the grid category of MVTec AD, ThermalCLIP achieves an image-level AUROC of 0.9942 compared to 0.6817 for PatchCore under identical evaluation conditions, a gap that no appearance-based method is positioned to close. Across all 15 MVTec AD categories, ThermalCLIP achieves a mean image level AUROC of 0.9441, and 0.8724 in zero-shot transfer to the VisA dataset. The complete framework runs at 7.5 FPS on a consumer-grade GPU with no infrared sensor required.
title: ThermalCLIP: Hardware-Agnostic Industrial Anomaly Detection via Physics-Informed Thermal Proxies from RGB

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Effective pest and disease detection plays a crucial role in minimizing crop losses and improving decision-making in precision agriculture. Among the most destructive pests affecting maize crops globally is the Fall Army Worm (FAW), known for its rapid spread and high impact on yield. Existing detection practices often rely on manual scouting, which can be inefficient, labour intensive and prone to human error. This study proposes a novel deep learning based framework for the automatic classification of FAW infested and healthy maize crops by integrating RGB and thermal image modalities. The core objective is to enhance detection accuracy through multimodal image fusion. A hybrid DNN-ViT model is introduced, combining two complimentary pipelines: (i) feature-level fusion, where CNN extracted features from RGB and thermal images are fused and classified using a Deep Neural Network (DNN) and (ii) image-level fusion, where a 6 channel RGB-thermal image is directly processed using a modified Vision Transformer (ViT). Experimental results demonstrate that the fused model achieved superior performance with an accuracy of 0.98, precision, recall and F1-score of 0.98 and AUC-ROC of 0.98 on the test set, outperforming models trained on RGB-only, thermal-only and unfused data. The ablation study confirms the effectiveness of multimodal fusion, with the no-fusion model showing significantly lower performance (accuracy-0.60 and AUC-ROC-0.67). This work highlights the benefits of integrating complementary data sources for robust crop health monitoring. Future research will explore enhanced fusion strategies, environmental robustness and field level deployment to validate the model’s practical applicability.</jats:p>
title: Robust Fall Army Worm detection in maize using multimodal RGB and thermal image fusion

items.abstract: Wood surface defect detection is critical for guaranteeing product quality in intelligent manufacturing. However, it remains highly challenging due to complex wood-grain background interference, extreme scale variations, blurred defect boundaries, and irregular defect morphologies. To address these issues, this paper proposes GADE-YOLO, a geometry-adaptive network for industrial wood surface defect detection based on YOLOv11n. Specifically, for the issues of severe texture noise interference and blurred micro-defect edges, we design an adaptive multi-scale feature enhancement module (AMFE), which dynamically selects multi-scale receptive fields and leverages spatial attention to filter out wood-grain noise. Meanwhile, an adapted multi-scale edge enhancement module (MEEM) is embedded into the high-resolution layer to strengthen boundary perception and sharpen the blurred boundaries of tiny defects. To tackle geometric misalignment caused by fixed-grid convolution on irregular contours, we introduce the C3k2_DCN unit with modulated deformable convolution for adaptive spatial sampling. Furthermore, we construct a geometry-adaptive fusion network (GAFN) with triple-branch feature aggregation (TFA) to extend the feature pyramid to the P6 layer, optimize cross-scale information flow, mitigate semantic dilution and adapt to large-span defects. Extensive experiments on a self-built industrial wood defect dataset demonstrate that GADE-YOLO achieves 83.6% precision, 75.7% recall and 84.9% mAP@0.5, outperforming the baseline YOLOv11n by 6.4, 4.7 and 7.3 percentage points, respectively. Meanwhile, GADE-YOLO has 5.6 GFLOPs of computational complexity, maintaining the advantages of lightweight design and efficient parameterization. In addition, GADE-YOLO improves mAP@0.5 by 9.7 percentage points over YOLOv11n on the public wood defect dataset, demonstrating its feasibility, robustness, and potential for real-time industrial deployment.
title: GADE-YOLO: An Efficient Geometry-Adaptive Network for Industrial Wood Surface Defect Inspection

items.abstract: <jats:p>Blind image restoration is essential for machine vision–based surface defect inspection in modern manufacturing. Transparent and glossy components often suffer from hybrid blur, sensor noise, low light, and poor contrast, which obscure defects like scratches, pits, and bubbles, hindering automated detection. Most existing methods address only single degradations or idealized cases, lacking practical solutions for complex industrial environments. We propose SPGR-Net, a semantic prompt– and graph–guided blind restoration network designed as a preprocessing module for industrial defect inspection. It features a Degradation-Perceptive Prompt Module that uses CLIP-based vision-language alignment to infer degradation semantics and generate spatially adaptive soft prompts for patch-level restoration. A Graph-based Restoration Inference Module builds lightweight, degradation-aware spatial graphs and performs localized message passing. A hybrid backbone combining convolutional blocks, Mamba-based state-space layers, and lightweight Transformers improves both restoration quality and efficiency. We introduce the Industrial Hybrid Degradation Dataset (IHDD), containing real and synthetic degradations from transparent injection-molded parts, and evaluate SPGR-Net on IHDD using standard metrics. SPGR-Net surpasses state-of-the-art all-in-one restoration methods in PSNR, SSIM, and perceptual quality. When integrated into a YOLOv9-based defect detection pipeline on IHDD, it increases mAP from 55.9\% to 89.97\% and F1 score from 0.58 to 0.91. These results show that semantic prompting and graph reasoning enable effective blind restoration, offering a robust solution for real-world industrial applications.</jats:p>
title: Blind Industrial Image Restoration with Semantic Prompting and Graph Reasoning for Surface Defect Inspection
